findings.text: Four maintenance passes are bypassed by direct guards that never reach _global_maintenance_call, so they are named in no log line and absent from the receipt, while the aggregate line reports 'count=24' as the run's bypass summary. Triggering input: sn run --scope-run-id <id> (skip_global_maintenance=True). Measured at the integrated head by running the scoped loop and differencing the receipt against the repo's own enumeration in tests/standard_names/test_scoped_global_maintenance._bypassed_maintenance_writers: RECEIPT_COUNT 24, ASSERTED_BYPASSED_COUNT 28, SILENTLY_BYPASSED ['embed_description_worker', 'mark_orphaned_standard_name_runs_stale', 'reconcile_attachment_consistency', 'restamp_harmonized_families']. The four sites are loop.py:1633 (mark_orphaned_standard_name_runs_stale), loop.py:2319 (embed_description_worker task never created), loop.py:2755 (rederive_structural_edges, normalize_derived_parent_lifecycle, reconcile_orphan_parent_sources called directly via asyncio.to_thread - their names appear in the receipt from earlier helper-routed sites, so this second skipped execution is masked), loop.py:2810 (restamp_harmonized_families). reconcile_attachment_consistency has its own bespoke log line at loop.py:1274 but is absent from the structured list. Fix: route these through _global_maintenance_call, or record them explicitly; the aggregate line should not present count=24 as total when it is a subset. Probe and log: receipt-totality-probe.py / receipt-totality-probe.log in this review run's directory.

The new pin is bypassable on an input the test does not construct: it asserts summary.bypassed_maintenance_passes equals a hardcoded 24-name tuple, which is satisfied by adding a fifth direct 'if not skip_global_maintenance:' guard anywhere in run_sn_pools - the receipt stays exactly 24 and the suite stays green while another pass goes silent. That is how the four existing omissions arrived. Triggering input: add any new maintenance call under a direct skip guard. The assertion that would have caught it already exists one import away: the test module it imports exposes _bypassed_maintenance_writers, and asserting set(_bypassed_maintenance_writers(mocks)) <= set(summary.bypassed_maintenance_passes) fails today with the four names above. A second gap: the test sets __name__ on every mock before the run, so the 'else type(fn).__name__' fallback added by 87916b6e5 is never executed by any test in the repo.

The hasattr-based callable-name lookup never raises for any object - type(fn).__name__ always exists - and is correct for all 24 current call sites, every one of which passes a plain module-level function. It is not total in the sense of yielding a usable name for the shapes the gate names. Measured: plain function -> 'real_pass'; functools.partial(fn) -> 'partial'; lambda -> '<lambda>'; bound method Holder().reconcile -> 'reconcile' with no class qualifier; bare MagicMock -> 'MagicMock'. Triggering input: wrapping loop.py:2047 refresh_drifted_sources (which already passes scope_run_id as a keyword) in functools.partial - the receipt would read 'partial' and, with two such sites, 'partial, partial'. Not a defect in the landed code; recorded so the next caller does not discover it by reading a useless receipt. functools.partial exposes .func, so an explicit unwrap is the fix if partials are ever introduced.

Outside this node's write scope, reported not fixed. Both operator-visible channels for the new receipt can be off simultaneously in a default rich sn run. sn.py:923 sets propagate=False on 'imas_codex.standard_names' whenever use_rich; the auto-log RotatingFileHandler is attached to the 'imas_codex' logger (cli/logging.py:158-174), so propagation stops before reaching it. Demonstrated here: with propagate=False set on that logger, a subsequent loop-logger INFO record leaves the file-handler output containing only the pre-suppression line. Meanwhile the printed summary table at sn.py:1006-1018 iterates a fixed key allowlist that omits bypassed_maintenance_passes. Triggering input: sn run --scope-run-id <id> with rich display, i.e. the default. The receipt then survives only in the returned row dict for a programmatic caller; the run's own log file on disk does not carry it. Adding 'bypassed_maintenance_passes' to the printed key tuple is the one-line fix and makes the receipt independent of the logging architecture.

justifications.durability: The new invariant does NOT hold at every construction site, and the gap is the same class of defect the node was dispatched to close. Four sites bypass maintenance work with a direct guard instead of the helper, so nothing names them: loop.py:1633 'if not skip_global_maintenance:' calling mark_orphaned_standard_name_runs_stale through a plain import; loop.py:2319 'if not skip_global_maintenance:' which simply never creates the embed_description_worker task; loop.py:2755 'if not reconcile_only and not skip_global_maintenance:' which calls rederive_structural_edges, normalize_derived_parent_lifecycle and reconcile_orphan_parent_sources directly via asyncio.to_thread - those three names DO appear in the receipt from their earlier helper-routed sites, so their second skipped execution is masked by a name already present; and loop.py:2810 'if not names_only and not skip_global_maintenance:' skipping restamp_harmonized_families. The node's test constructs none of these: it asserts equality against a hardcoded 24-name tuple, so ADDING a fifth direct-bypass guard tomorrow leaves the suite green and the receipt silently short - the guard is bypassable on an input the node's own tests do not construct. Separately, the receipt's only operator-visible channels can both be off at once. sn.py:923 sets propagate=False on 'imas_codex.standard_names' whenever use_rich, and the auto-log RotatingFileHandler is attached to the 'imas_codex' logger (cli/logging.py:158), so propagation stops before it - demonstrated here: a record emitted after that assignment leaves the file log containing only the pre-suppression line. Meanwhile the printed summary table (sn.py:1006-1018) iterates a fixed key allowlist that does not include bypassed_maintenance_passes. So in a default rich sn run the 24 lines reach neither terminal nor ~/.local/share/imas-codex/logs, and the table never mentions the bypass; the receipt survives only in the returned row dict for a programmatic caller. Three wave questions answered: (1) the change cannot be wholly inverted with the suite green - the mutation log proves the pin fires - but a NEW silent bypass is green by construction; (2) the invariant does not hold at every site, four sites above; (3) one existing test did assert the replaced behaviour, test_attachment_audit.py:3199 'result == AttachmentAuditResult()', and this change correctly narrowed it to rejected == [] / detached == 0 / audit_ran is False.
justifications.evidence: The reproduction is real and could have failed. base-defect-reproductions.log at 6f81dc047 prints receipt_has_bypassed_maintenance_passes: False with named_bypass_logs holding only three pre-existing lines and none naming a maintenance function, plus a live RuntimeError('graph unavailable') traceback and audit_ran True / equals_default True for DEFECT 2 - the defect observed, not asserted. negative-control.log is well formed: first line 'MUTATION: removed per-pass bypass naming and receipt recording from _global_maintenance_call' verbatim, ending '1 failed' on tests/standard_names/test_bypassed_maintenance_is_named.py by name. The suite delta closes arithmetically: base and head both 20 FAILED + 3 ERROR = 23 identical ids, passes 7510 -> 7511 for the one test added. Re-run here at the integrated head over the five surface files: '96 passed, 20 deselected' exit 0 (focused-at-integrated-head.log). Docked twice. First, the node never measured its receipt against the repo's existing enumeration of bypassed writers, which sits in the very module its new test imports - _bypassed_maintenance_writers returns 28 names and the receipt has 24; one set-difference would have surfaced all four omissions. Second, the new test sets __name__ on every mock before the run, which arranges the input so the hasattr TRUE branch is always taken; no test in the repo exercises the 'else type(fn).__name__' fallback the corrective commit added, so that branch has zero coverage and zero mutation proof.
justifications.fit: The change does the right structural thing the previous review asked for: it extends the existing shared _global_maintenance_call rather than building a second parallel skip idiom beside it, so all 24 helper-routed passes gain the receipt from one edit, and the RunSummary field is appended last with a default_factory so no positional construction is disturbed (grep finds RunSummary built with keywords at all five sites). The aggregate line sits in the finally block at loop.py:2833, after both shutdown-path helper calls at 2726 and 2787 and after the reconcile_only early return at 2230, so it is reached on the normal, early-return, exception and KeyboardInterrupt paths alike. The attachment_audit.py one-word change to AttachmentAuditResult(audit_ran=False) in the except branch closes precisely the finding the prior review left open. Docked three times. First, the callable-name lookup is total in the sense that it never raises - type(fn).__name__ always exists - and is correct for all 24 current sites, every one of which passes a plain module-level function; but it degrades to a useless receipt for two of the three shapes the gate names. Measured: plain function -> 'real_pass', functools.partial -> 'partial', lambda -> '<lambda>', bound method -> 'reconcile' (bare, no class), bare MagicMock -> 'MagicMock'. Site 2047 already passes a keyword argument, so wrapping it in a partial is a plausible next refactor that would silently log 'partial'. Second, the new test imports a PRIVATE helper from a sibling test module (from tests.standard_names import test_scoped_global_maintenance) and monkeypatches its _maintenance_mocks; renaming that helper breaks the new test from another file with no compile-time link. Third, the receipt is a flat list of names with no count of executions, so the three post-drain repeats at loop.py:2755 are structurally unrepresentable in it.
